subject: Oceanography
title: Satellites and the Ocean
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Satellites and the Ocean.

hook.text: Satellites orbiting 700 km above Earth can measure ocean temperature accurate to 0.1°C.

buildup.text: Remote sensing lets scientists monitor the entire ocean surface continuously—something ships can't do.

discovery.text: Satellites track sea level rise, phytoplankton blooms, currents, ice cover, and surface winds.

twist.text: Satellite altimeters detect sea surface height so precisely they can map underwater mountains from orbit.

climax.text: Since the 1990s, satellite data has transformed oceanography from ship-based surveys to global science.

punchline.text: To see the whole ocean, you have to leave Earth.

quiz.question: What can satellite altimeters detect about the ocean?
options: Underwater features via sea surface height changes
